summary.headline: Mankind Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to INR3,443 crores with adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.1%; FY27 guided to double-digit growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.8% YoY to INR3,443 crores, led by 13.4% domestic growth, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 400 bps to 27.1% on better gross margin, operating leverage and a lower Q4 base. Full-year FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR14,278 crores, but PAT fell 3.4% to INR1,938 crores as finance cost, depreciation and lower other income weighed. Management said acute therapies were muted during FY26 but recovered sequentially from Q2, and chronic share rose to about 39-40%. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of at least double digits and adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.5-26.5%, with an effective tax rate stepping up to 25-26%.

segments.name: Domestic formulations (ex-Consumer Healthcare)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 12.9% per management's first remark (13.4% on domestic revenue of INR2,886 crores), with organic ex-OTC growth of 10.1%, the highest since the BSV acquisition. FY26 domestic revenue INR12,217 crores, +14.4%.

segments.name: Chronic therapies
segments.commentary: Chronic share about 40% in Q4 (+120 bps YoY) and about 39% for FY26 (+190 bps). Outperformed IPM 1.1x in cardiac and 1.6x in anti-diabetes ex-GLP-1 in FY26, but Q4 was 0.9x IPM per analyst's question, which management did not dispute.

segments.name: Acute therapies
segments.commentary: Gastro outperformed IPM at 1.1x (Pantakind 1.4x); gynaecology +10.8% with Dydrogesterone +20%; vitamins and minerals +12.5%. Management expects acute to grow in line with IPM in FY27.

segments.name: BSV specialty (domestic)
segments.commentary: Strong double-digit growth led by Anti-D, Foligraf (+52%) and HMG (+40%). Management says secondary sales for the brand are growing in mid-teens.

segments.name: Consumer Healthcare / OTC
segments.commentary: Q4 OTC revenue INR213 crores (+20%), with modern trade and e-commerce +57%. Share of e-commerce and modern trade rose from about 9% in FY25 to 13% in FY26. FY26 OTC INR879 crores (+9%).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 exports INR557 crores (+4%), hit by geopolitical headwinds and BSV exposure in LATAM, RCIS and the Philippines. FY26 international INR2,061 crores (+35%). Management expects high double-digit growth in FY27 for both international business units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at double digits or better, with aspiration to outperform IPM (IQVIA).
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided at 25.5% to 26.5%, better than FY26's 25.4%, with caveats on geopolitics and market conditions.
FY27 effective tax rate expected at 25% to 26%, up from 15-16% in FY26, as the Sikkim tax exemption ends.
Capex guidance of 6% to 7% of FY27 revenue, driven by the new Vadodara biotech facility; board approved up to INR500 crores investment in Mankind Medicare for this.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA expected at 0.5x for FY27; acquisition-related debt to be repaid by FY28. Next repayment INR1,250 crores in October 2026, and INR2,500 crores due in FY27.
Employee cost targeted at around 22% of sales over the long term (plus/minus 0.5%).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR737 crores (5.2% of revenue); FY27 capex guided at 6-7% of revenue.
New best-in-class biotech facility under construction in Vadodara, aligned with R&D and specialty focus.
Udaipur and Ambernath facilities received EU GMP certification during FY26, supporting semi-regulated market entry.
Board approved investment of up to INR500 crores in subsidiary Mankind Medicare for the Vadodara biotech plant; spend phased into the coming year.
demand_pricing: Price increase for FY26 was 4.2% per IQVIA versus about 4.4% for the industry.
Q4 IQVIA secondary sales growth 8.7% vs IPM 10.7% ex-GLP-1; muted anti-infective, with recovery in gastro, gynae, vitamins and derma QoQ.
Prescription share 15.1% and prescriber penetration 84.1%; ranked number 1 in prescriptions for the ninth consecutive year.
GLP-1: pen launched about one month before the call, targeting endocrinologists first; management said it is not launching vials or cutting prices.

Management attributed the Q2 onward recovery to acute therapies after corrective actions, with Q2, Q3 and Q4 growing sequentially. Raw material, packaging and excipient costs are disrupted due to the Middle East conflict; management said precautions were taken but gave no quantified impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is the disruption in sales teams behind us and is domestic business back to normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Juneja said corrections are done and the company is on the path to recovery; chronic (38-40% of sales) was not hit, only acute was.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-line growth guided to double digits, with aspiration to outperform IQVIA; EBITDA margin guided at 25.5-26.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q4 chronic outperformance only 0.9x IPM, and what is driving the high Q4 margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Sheetal Arora said there is no chronic pressure. Ashutosh Dhawan attributed the margin to a 60 bps gross margin gain, operating leverage, a Q4 FY25 relaunch base effect and a commission waiver.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall sequentially and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost fell 9% QoQ: about 5-5.5% from lower revenue, incentives and true-up, and about 3.5% from waiver of director and commission fees. Normalised for BSV, annual employee cost rose about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will GLP-1 launch and base diabetes be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management launched a pen only, is not in a hurry for vials or price cuts, and is focusing on adjacent vitamins, minerals and protein. Sudipta Roy said there has been no direct impact yet on base anti-diabetic and cardiac therapies.

qa_highlights.question: How is the price hike and growth built into FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited recovery in acute, sustained chronic outperformance, and specialty and GLP-1 contribution. Price hikes were in line with industry at 4.2% vs 4.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BSV acquisition playing out as expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Juneja said BSV brought biologicals and complex products and that the domestic leadership change has worked, with the Philippines leadership also changed. He added that the company is 18-19 months into integration and that it took longer than planned.

risks_watch: Acute therapy recovery: management says acute grew muted in FY26 after corrective actions and expects it to match IPM in FY27; watch sequential acute growth against IQVIA data.
Chronic outperformance slowed to 0.9x IPM in Q4 FY26 from 1.1x for the full year; an analyst challenged this and management attributed it to no chronic pressure, so track quarterly chronic share.
Raw material, packaging and excipient cost disruption from the Middle East conflict; management gave no quantified margin impact, and FY27 EBITDA guidance of 25.5-26.5% is caveated for geopolitics.
Effective tax rate steps up to 25-26% in FY27 from 15-16% in FY26 as the Sikkim exemption ends, a sizeable drag on PAT growth.

International: BSV exposure in LATAM, RCIS and the Philippines hit Q4 exports (+4%); high double-digit FY27 growth is expected and needs to be verified. Debt repayments of INR1,250 crores in October 2026 and INR2,500 crores in FY27, plus capex of 6-7% of FY27 revenue, are the cash items to monitor.
GLP-1 pen launched about a month before the call with no vials or price cuts; watch uptake and any impact on base anti-diabetic and cardiac therapies, which management says is not yet visible.
key_quotes: So I can say only one thing that growth would be better -- top line growth will be better than the last year, double digit.
There is no pressure on chronic therapies because it's a long-term growth story.
Acute therapy would be in the line of IPM growth.
We are not in a hurry to launch vials. We are not in a hurry to cut down the prices.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the recovery and FY27 outlook, citing the Q2-to-Q4 sequential improvement and a commitment to hold margins, but it was cautious and at times evasive on specifics. It gave no quantified raw-material impact, declined to split export growth between Mankind and BSV, and caveated the EBITDA guidance for geopolitics and market conditions.

adds.what: New best-in-class biotech facility in Vadodara (under construction), up to INR500 crore investment via Mankind Medicare

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at double digits or better (aspiration to outperform IQVIA), with Q4 revenue +11.8% and FY26 +17%; delivery backed by share gains, international high double-digit growth guidance and BSV momentum, but no quantified order book or capacity addition for FY27 revenue, so backing is partial.
